thread:
sophie: Heads upnoticed weird numbers on the latency dashboard. Top-level p99 for /v2/embed is 420ms but the endpoint breakdown for ap-south shows p99 ~920ms. Refresh didn't help.

vik: Oof. Are the sample counts different between views? That usually explains t-digest edges.

sophie: Yes: top view sample_count=18.5k, ap-south slice sample_count=310.

tara: That's low. t-digest merging can give biased tails when tiny slices merge into big aggregates. We saw this with the canary a while ago.

mike: Can you paste the quick query?

sophie: Query:
```
select region, sample_count, p50, p95, p99 from latency_rollups
where endpoint='/v2/embed' and ts >= 1719299800 and ts <= 1719300000;
-- results: global 18500 45 120 420
-- ap-south 310 48 210 920
```

vik: That gap plus the tiny slice screams routing fallback or variant mismatch. Check routing events around 1719299900-1719299950.

tara: I'll tail the routing events. If quota fallback routed some traffic to a cpu-encoded model that would explain the large p99 localized to that region.

logs-bot: Routing: fallback event detected for tenant=shopify, route=/v2/embed, at=1719299937, reason=reserved_capacity_throttle, fallback_target=cpu-quantized-1

mike: Yep, fallback shows up. That means a concentrated tail in a small slice. In main rollup it's diluted by many other regions.

sophie: From Product POV this is confusing for on-callers: they look at top-level p99 and assume all good, but a critical region sees a big tail. Need a UX change so this mismatch is obvious.

vik: UX proposals: 1) show sample_count inline next to each percentile on the top-level card, 2) surface a "skewed" badge when a single slice contributes >40% of p99 mass, 3) add vertical annotation when routing fallback events occur.

tara: +1. Also a short tooltip: "Percentiles are from merged t-digests. Low-count slices can distort tail values. Click for per-slice breakdown." Link to docs.

mike: Infra angle: we should consider falling back to computing percentiles from raw samples for any slice where sample_count < 1000 before merging into dashboard comparatives. That avoids misleadings in low-sample regimes. I'll file INFRA-4302.

vik: Short-term: can we land the UI badge + tooltip fast? Low-risk. I'll open a tiny PR and canary it.

vik: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/851 (adds sample_count badge + skew indicator + tooltip)

tara: I'll add the dashboard annotation hook so routing fallback events emit an annotation band. That will make it obvious when a spike lines up with a quota action.

logs-bot: Deploy scheduled: console PR #851 canary -> 10% in 10m.

sophie: Thanks. Can we also add a short runbook blurb: "When percentiles disagree across views: check sample_count, inspect routing fallback events, query per-caller slices."

mike: Filing INFRA-4302: "raw-sample fallback for low-count slices when computing dashboard percentiles" with suggested threshold=1000 and test cases.

vik: Action items:
- vik: land UI badge + tooltip (console#851)
- tara: add routing-fallback annotation integration
- mike: INFRA-4302 + tests + alerts when slice sample_count < threshold for SLO charts
- sophie: update runbook + example queries

Follow-up: meet back at 1719300600 to verify numbers and close out. :thumbsup:
